report.summary: Chunk 4 of 6 of attempt.py: contains _contained_gate_child, command_gate, pytest_gate, offload_runner, and TaskAttempt.__init__ with docstrings and implementation.

symbols.name: _contained_gate_child
symbols.note: Launches gate at Low integrity, sets up worktree, temp dir, and output log.

symbols.name: command_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate callable that runs an arbitrary command inside the candidate worktree, with containment.

symbols.name: pytest_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate callable that runs pytest via command_gate.

symbols.name: offload_runner
symbols.note: Returns a runner callable that delegates to daedalus.offload.offload.

symbols.name: TaskAttempt
symbols.note: Produce one candidate change for one task, outside the primary checkout.

symbols.name: TaskAttempt.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes TaskAttempt with task, runner, and optional gate/ledger/cancel/worktree_manager.

claims.text: Three things are set up, and each is a measured requirement rather than tidiness: 1. THE WORKTREE IS LABELLED LOW... 2. A LOW-LABELLED TEMP DIRECTORY... 3. THE OUTPUT FILE IS CREATED AND LABELLED BY US, then opened append-only, and exactly that one handle is allowlisted into the child.
claims.why: The function calls containment.label_low_integrity(worktree), creates low_temp and labels it, opens log via containment.open_low_append_log(out_path), and passes log to spawn_contained.

claims.text: THE GATE IS WHERE CANDIDATE CODE ACTUALLY RUNS. Everything else in this module handles the candidate's bytes; this command executes them. So by default the child is launched at LOW INTEGRITY through daedalus.spine.containment, and the kernel -- not our path checks -- refuses the writes that a Python guard provably cannot close (the 'move-in' attack among them).
claims.why: In the _gate closure, if executes_candidate is True, it calls _contained_gate_child which labels worktree low and spawns contained. Otherwise it runs uncontained.

claims.text: THERE IS NO contained=False. A caller whose runner cannot produce candidate code says so with executes_candidate=False, which is a statement about the WORKLOAD and reads as one in a diff.
claims.why: command_gate has parameter executes_candidate (default True), no contained parameter.

claims.text: When containment cannot be established -- wrong platform, labelling refused, a handle that would not verify -- the gate REFUSES: passed=False with the reason in the output and in the attestation.
claims.why: In _gate, if executes_candidate and _contained_gate_child raises ContainmentUnavailable, refusal is set and GateResult returned with passed=False.

claims.text: Both children run inside a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a cancelled attempt kills the whole process TREE rather than the immediate child
claims.why: The code uses ManagedProcess which may set up job object, but that class is defined elsewhere; not in this chunk.

claims.text: Output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree: a pipe would deadlock on a chatty run while we are polling the cancel token instead of reading.
claims.why: Output is written to out_path (inside tmpdir, which is outside worktree) via log or stdout file handle.

claims.text: Under containment that file is the ONE handle inherited by the child, opened append-only on a Low-labelled target and verified on the handle.
claims.why: The log is opened via containment.open_low_append_log, but its implementation and verification are not in this chunk.

claims.text: That scratch directory is then removed through the GUARDED walker, not shutil.rmtree -- it lives in %TEMP% under a prefix named in this file while candidate code is running as this user, so it is a delete against attacker-reachable ground like every other delete in this system.
claims.why: _remove_gate_tmpdir is called but not defined in this chunk; guarded walker not visible.

claims.text: A gate that exits 0 having produced NOTHING has not judged anything -- something ate the evidence.
claims.why: After polling, if passed and not output.strip(), passed is set to False and output replaced with a warning.

claims.text: Run the repository's pytest gate through command_gate.
repo_root is pinned to the WORKTREE, so offload's snapshot / verify / rollback machinery operates entirely inside the isolated checkout.
claims.why: In _runner, kwargs.pop('repo_root', None) removes any user-supplied repo_root, and offload is called with str(ctx.worktree).

claims.text: Deliberately not the default: TaskAttempt refuses to construct without an explicit runner, so no attempt can quietly reach a model because a caller forgot an argument.
claims.why: TaskAttempt.__init__ requires runner parameter and raises ValueError if not callable.

claims.text: run() NEVER applies its result. There is no code path in this class that writes the primary working tree -- see the module docstring for the three properties that make that structural rather than promised.
claims.why: run() method not present in this chunk; module docstring not included.

observations.what: In _contained_gate_child, after spawning proc, if an exception occurs, log is closed and re-raised. However, if proc is spawned successfully but later code fails, proc is not explicitly closed (though it may be managed elsewhere).

In command_gate's _gate, when executes_candidate is False, ManagedProcess is used without containment; docstring claims 'Both children run inside a Job Object' but uncontained child may not have that guarantee.
TaskAttempt.__init__ imports from daedalus.eval.correctness inside an elif branch, which may cause circular import at module level but is safe at runtime.
